results.title: Fix Broken Chassis Before Implementing AI in Finance | Naqqash Abbassi posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content:
I spoke to a CFO who is under pressure from his CEO to implement AI. "Where do I start?" he asked. My answer surprised him:
Fix your invoice approval workflow first.
He went quiet.
He'd expected me to say forecasting tools. Maybe board reporting dashboards. Something strategic enough to put in front of the CEO. Not invoice approvals.
Here's what I've learned after 4 years inside finance teams. The CFOs getting real results from AI didn't start with the intelligent part. They started with the broken part.
His team was manually matching invoices to purchase orders. Chasing approvals over email. Reconciling payments in a spreadsheet on the last day of the month. Copying data between systems that were never designed to talk to each other.
That is the chassis. And it was broken. [...] Most CFOs wait until the AI strategy is perfect before deploying anything.
The data is never clean enough. The process is never fully documented. The governance framework isn't signed off yet.
So they wait.
Meanwhile the CFO at the company down the road automated their AP process in 6 weeks with messy data, an incomplete process map, and no governance framework.
It wasn't perfect. It worked.
Here's what I've learned after 4 years deploying AI for finance teams:
The CFOs who get results are not the ones who planned the best. They're the ones who started before they were ready.
They picked one workflow. Ran it imperfectly. Fixed what broke. Then expanded.
The CFOs still waiting for perfect conditions are not being careful. They're being slow. Those are not the same thing. [...] The CFOs getting real results from AI didn't start with the intelligent part. They started with the broken part. The invoice that gets manually coded. The reconciliation that runs in a spreadsheet at month-end.
The approval that lives in someone's inbox for 11 days.
Fix those first and something surprising happens.
The forecasting gets more accurate. The board reporting gets faster. The strategic conversations get easier.
Not because you added AI to strategy.
Because you fixed the data that strategy runs on.
The back office is not where AI goes last.
It's where AI has to go first.
